# Acts of Thomas — Chapter 6
**Agent:** SOPHIA (Consensus)
**Source:** Syriac MS / Greek recension, Acts of Thomas 6

---

## Consensus Translation

*[Exorcism of a young woman. The demon's involuntary testimony.]*

1. As Thomas was traveling through cities and villages, he encountered a young woman who was afflicted and tormented by a demon.

2. She came to Thomas and fell at his feet, saying: "I beg you, servant of God — have compassion on me and pray for me, that I may be freed from this demon who torments and afflicts me."

3. Thomas said to her: "What torments does this demon inflict upon you? Tell me."

4. She said: "He takes on every manner of form before me, and when he wishes to trouble me, he appears as a man."

5. Thomas said: "Tell me — how long has this demon been tormenting you?"

6. She said: "From my youth. He has pursued me and greatly afflicted me."

7. Thomas prayed over her, and the demon was cast out and cried as it departed: "Woe to you, Thomas! You were born at the same moment Christ was born, and you have always troubled us."

8. Thomas said: "Be silent, spirit of affliction and deceit."

9. The demon departed.

10. The woman glorified God and attached herself to Thomas, serving him and ministering to all his needs.

11. Thomas said to her: "Go home, daughter. The Lord will keep you and guard you from all evil."

12. She departed, glorifying God.

13. Many who witnessed this believed, and they came and were baptized in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit.

---

## Textual Notes

- **"Born at the same moment Christ was born" (v.7):** The demon's involuntary confession is the theological heart of the chapter. In demonic testimony — a recognized category in early Christian exorcism tradition — the truth is spoken against the demon's will. The Thomas-as-twin-of-Christ tradition (Syriac) is grounded here.
- **"Spirit of affliction and deceit" (v.8):** Thomas's rebuke names both the demon's mode of operation — it afflicts (produces suffering) and deceives (takes many forms). The naming is part of the exorcistic command.
- **"Attached herself to Thomas, serving him" (v.10):** A common pattern in the Acts of Thomas — those healed become disciples. Women who follow Thomas form a community around him throughout the narrative.
- **Trinitarian baptismal formula (v.13):** The full Matthean formula (Matt 28:19). Used consistently throughout the ATH at conversion moments.

---
*SOPHIA synthesis: Chapter 6 follows the standard exorcism-to-conversion pattern but is distinguished by the demon's involuntary testimony about Thomas's divine identity. Preserved in full.*
